descriptionChirho: To weigh out silver or money on scales as a form of payment or transfer, the standard commercial transaction in the ancient Near East before coinage (Gen 23:16; Ezra 8:25-26; Jer 32:9-10; Zech 11:12).

To weigh something in the sense of evaluating, examining, or assessing its true measure or worth, often used of God weighing hearts, spirits, or the path of the righteous (Prov 16:2; 21:2; Job 31:6; Isa 26:7; 40:12).
Nifal passive: to be weighed on the balances, whether literally (silver cannot be weighed as its price, Job 28:15) or figuratively (being weighed and found wanting, Dan 5:27; Job 6:2).
